तस्य पराक्रमः इव पराक्रमः येषां ते
samasa.sense: as strong in battle as he

morph.note: Perfect of √स्रु: reduplication सु-स्राव, with vṛddhi of the root vowel in the third singular.
Perfect of √स्था (तस्थुः ‘they stood’) with सम् + उद्: उद् + स्था loses the s of the root (उत्था-), so उत्-तस्थुः. ‘They rose up together’.
Genitive of the past participle, without a noun: ‘of (him) struck’. It names the source of the blood.

mantras.anvaya: कुलिशेन आहतस्य (तस्य) आशु बहु शोणितं सुस्राव; ततः तद्रूपाः तत्पराक्रमाः योधाः समुत्तस्थुः।
mantras.lit: From him, struck by the thunderbolt, much blood flowed at once; from it rose up warriors of his form and his prowess.
mantras.tr: Struck by the thunderbolt, he bled at once and freely, and from that blood rose warriors with his form and his strength.

comm.t: The rule of 8.41 is now seen working: the first wound fills the field with Raktabīja’s doubles. ततः can be ‘then’ or ‘from it’; both fit, since the warriors rise from the blood.

mantras.anvaya: तस्य शरीरात् यावन्तः रक्तबिन्दवः पतिताः, तावन्तः तद्वीर्यबलविक्रमाः पुरुषाः जाताः।
mantras.anvaya_en: A यावत् … तावत् sentence of quantity.
mantras.lit: As many drops of blood as fell from his body, so many men were born with his valour, strength and prowess.
mantras.tr: For every drop of blood that fell from his body a warrior was born, with his valour, his strength and his prowess.
mantras.tr_note: ‘For every … a’ renders the correlatives ‘as many … so many’.

comm.t: The narrator states the arithmetic of the danger: one drop, one Raktabīja. Each copy has not only his shape (8.43) but his full power.

samasa.literal: those whose origin is from blood

samasa.members: अति + उग्र + शस्त्र + पात + अति + भीषण
samasa.vigraha: अत्युग्राणि शस्त्राणि अत्युग्रशस्त्राणि; तेषां पातः अत्युग्रशस्त्रपातः; तेन अतिभीषणम्
samasa.type: tṛtīyā tatpuruṣa containing a ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa and a karmadhāraya (अत्युग्रशस्त्र, whose first member अत्युग्र is a prādi compound)
samasa.literal: exceedingly terrible through the falling of exceedingly fierce weapons
samasa.sense: a fight made dreadful by a rain of savage blows
samasa.alt: It may also qualify an understood cognate object युद्धम् (‘fought a battle most terrible …’); the meaning is the same.

morph.note: √युध् is an ātmanepada root (8.42 युयुधे); the classical third plural would be युयुधिरे. युयुधुः, with the parasmaipada ending, is an epic (ārṣa) form that the Purāṇas use freely.
A long compound in the neuter accusative singular serving as an adverb of manner: ‘(fought) in a manner most terrible with …’.

mantras.anvaya: ते रक्तसम्भवाः पुरुषाः च अपि तत्र मातृभिः समम् अत्युग्रशस्त्रपातातिभीषणं युयुधुः।
mantras.lit: And those men too, born of the blood, fought there with the Mothers, most terribly with the fall of very fierce weapons.
mantras.tr: The warriors born of the blood fought the Mothers too, a battle made terrible by the crash of savage weapons.

comm.t: The doubles do not merely appear; they fight, and the Mothers now face an army that grows with every wound they inflict.

samasa.sense: by a stroke of Aindrī’s vajra

morph.note: Perfect of √वह् with reduplication व-वाह. Used here of the wounded head ‘carrying’ blood, i.e. streaming with it.
Past participle of √क्षण् (the nasal is lost before -त): क्षत ‘wounded’, here a predicate with आसीत् understood.

mantras.anvaya: पुनः च यदा वज्रपातेन अस्य शिरः क्षतम् (आसीत्), (तदा तत्) रक्तं ववाह; ततः सहस्रशः पुरुषाः जाताः।
mantras.lit: And again, when his head was wounded by the fall of the thunderbolt, it poured out blood; from that men were born by thousands.
mantras.tr: Again the thunderbolt struck and wounded his head; the blood poured out, and from it warriors were born in their thousands.

comm.t: A second stroke of the vajra, to the head this time. The numbers rise from hundreds to thousands: each blow makes the problem worse.

sandhi_exceptions.reason: Hiatus at the pāda break (गदया ताडयामास is a full pāda of eight syllables): the a of ताडयामास is not fused with the ai of ऐन्द्री (which would give ताडयामासैन्द्री). A licence of epic verse, which may treat the pāda boundary as a pause; the text is printed so in the Gita Press.

mantras.anvaya: वैष्णवी च समरे एनं चक्रेण अभिजघान ह; ऐन्द्री तम् असुरेश्वरं गदया ताडयामास।
mantras.lit: And Vaiṣṇavī indeed struck him in battle with the discus; Aindrī struck that lord of the asuras with a mace.
mantras.tr: Vaiṣṇavī struck him in battle with her discus, and Aindrī struck the asura lord with a mace.

comm.t: Two Mothers attack together. The text gives Aindrī a mace (गदा) here, where earlier she used her thunderbolt (8.42, 8.46); the Gita Press reading is kept as it stands.

flags.uncertain: गदया with ऐन्द्री: Aindrī’s weapon elsewhere in the chapter is the vajra. corrections.json logs no variant for this verse; the mace is translated as written.
